calls.title: Gifthealth x GrowthBook: Enablement Session
calls.summary: The team focused on a structured approach to experimentation, beginning with single-factor tests to promote clarity and discipline, as highlighted by Elizabeth Gilbert due to low familiarity with experimentation in the company. Cris Dizon emphasized iterative testing via decision trees as an effective alternative to more complex multifactor designs, which will be adopted as traffic volume and context allow. The initial prioritization framework will utilize a simple effort-impact quadrant for experiment selection, while emphasizing clear decision criteria for various outcomes. Transitioning to overlapping experiments is planned using Growth Book’s logic to maximize efficiency, with attention given to memory-related technical challenges due to excessive auto slices. Knowledge-sharing resources will be developed to support ongoing learning and process improvement.
calls.keywords: Experimentation, A/B Testing, Minimum Detectable Effect, Prioritization Framework, Overlapping Experiments, Memory Error
calls.action_items:
**Cris Dizon**
Share slides detailing the effort vs. impact prioritization framework and advanced test design strategies with Elizabeth (08:21)
Provide detailed slides explaining hashing and randomization processes for overlapping experiments and finalize them for sharing (33:14)
Send Google Doc version of Elizabeth's experiment guides with comments to continue asynchronous collaboration (47:03)
Follow up on checking if there is a built-in tool for verifying randomization balance across overlapping experiments and report findings (28:08)

**Elizabeth Gilbert**
Add a column to the historical experiment repository to log actual collected MDE values per experiment for retrospective analysis (14:17)
Share the first three SQL queries related to the memory error issue with Chris and Cris for troubleshooting assistance (50:18)
Continue running the second experiment while monitoring for memory issues and traffic allocation concerns (16:19)

**Chris Sanders**
Review and analyze shared SQL queries to diagnose the memory error related to auto slices and provide remediation suggestions (50:20)
